clue.text: Spell single word for Scrabble's elementary rule

parts.note: a spell is a stretch of time, a period
single means one, the Roman numeral I
to scrabble is to scratch about, to claw

explanation.surface: A request for one word that sums up the basic rule of the board game Scrabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrabble' looks like the game's name; here it is the verb, to scratch at. 'Elementary' puns on the chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: The periodic law is the principle that orders the chemical elements, so it is literally a rule about elements.

clue.text: One on the road can, on Spice Girls tours

indicators.note: the letters go on a tour, travelling around into new positions

explanation.surface: A tin can is carried on the Spice Girls' tours.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican crossing is a pedestrian crossing with lights, a feature found on a road in the UK.

clue.text: Hoots from river, one owl primarily hollowed-out trees

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: first and foremost, so the opening letter of the bird is taken
with the inside scooped out, only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: An owl hoots from hollow trees by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoots' looks like owl calls; it means very funny things.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot, like a hoot, is something or someone hilariously funny.

clue.text: Over time, ridiculous to bury head in sand like this?

definitions.text: Over time, ridiculous to bury head in sand like this?

indicators.note: burying puts one thing deep inside another, so a letter goes into the middle

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
rich means absurd, as in 'that's rich'

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Over time, it seems ridiculous to hide your head in the sand, as a certain bird is said to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bury' puts the S from 'head in sand' inside O, T and RICH. The whole clue also describes the bird, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless bird is popularly, if wrongly, said to hide its head in sand when threatened.

clue.text: Senselessness of sick needing oxygen getting rolled-up cigarette

parts.note: sick means ill
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: in a down clue, rolled up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cig is a cigarette

explanation.surface: The pointlessness of smoking a roll-up when ill and needing oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogic is a lack of reasoning, the absence of sense.

clue.text: After hugging guys, one has regret

indicators.note: one word wraps round the other like an embrace

parts.note: after means later
guys means men

explanation.surface: Someone who hugged a few men regretted it afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamenter is a person who mourns or expresses sorrow.

clue.text: Teacher trained with software, Outlook

indicators.note: trained means reshaped or brought into a new form, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A teacher has been taught to use Outlook, the email software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlook' looks like Microsoft's email program; it means a forecast of what lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook is a prediction of coming conditions, as in a meteorological forecast.

clue.text: Buxom partner getting caught on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top means placed above, so it comes first

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hubby is informal for husband, a partner

explanation.surface: A plump partner is caught in a compromising position, on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Buxom and chubby both describe someone plump or well-rounded.

clue.text: Staff covering large garden at the back getting fertiliser

indicators.note: one word goes over and round the other

parts.note: a staff is a long stick, a pole

indicators.note: the very end of the word, its final letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A gardener uses a pole to spread fertiliser at the back of a big garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollen fertilises flowers, carrying male cells to the female parts of plants.

clue.text: Finish putting pickle away

parts.note: a pickle is a fix or awkward spot, a hole
away from home means out

explanation.surface: Instructions to stop storing something and put the jar of pickle back in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' looks like placing things; it is golf putting.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to sink the ball with the final stroke on a green completes the hole, ending the putting.

clue.text: Stack Beano at first with earlier back issue

indicators.note: joins the last piece onto the end of the others in this clue

parts.note: a lum is a Scottish word for a chimney stack

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the comic's name is used here

parts.note: earlier means ago, as in 'years ago'

explanation.surface: A collector piles up old copies of the Beano comic, including an earlier back issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back issue' looks like an old comic; it is a sore back. The Beano is a long-running British children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back, a medical problem of the back.

clue.text: First motion of club supports extension

parts.note: to support someone is to back them; he backs
a wing is an extension to a building

explanation.surface: A club gains backing for a new extension to its premises.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the stroke begins by drawing the club back and up before the downswing.

clue.text: Nothing cool for retirement? Chill naked

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so this word is turned round

parts.note: cool means fashionable, in

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, keeping the inside of the word

explanation.surface: Someone with nothing to do in retirement decides to relax without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nihil is Latin for nothing, used in English in phrases such as nihil obstat.

clue.text: American's a jerk

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a person from the United States

explanation.surface: An insult: the American is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is slang for an American and also a verb or noun for a hard tug.

clue.text: Scared to charge a pound for eggs

parts.note: chicken means cowardly, scared
to run something is to be in charge of it

explanation.surface: Someone is too timid to ask a whole pound for a box of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money; it is an enclosure, a pen for hens that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken run is a fenced enclosure where hens are kept, a pen for egg-layers.

clue.text: Trouble with endless Viagra, get off tablet

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
without an end, so the final letter of each word is removed

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Problems with an unfinished Viagra pill, and getting off a tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims both Viagra and get, giving VIAGR and GE; 'off' rearranges these, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to distress or wrong someone, to trouble them.

clue.text: Moneylenders mad at Rees-Mogg

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Bankers are furious with Jacob Rees-Mogg, a Conservative politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly mortgagees are the lenders who hold a mortgage over a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortgagees are the banks or lenders to whom a borrower's property is pledged.

clue.text: Flash Power's a floor cleaner

parts.note: a flash is a moment, a mo
a means per, as in 'ten pounds a head'

explanation.surface: Flash Power is the name of a cleaning product for floors.
explanation.walkthrough: Flash is a British brand of household cleaner, which makes 'Flash Power' read as a product name.
explanation.definitionFit: A mopper is a person or thing that mops, cleaning floors.

clue.text: Pop singer, mostly with guitarist Paul after good laughs

indicators.note: the rest comes after the first piece
most of the name, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Iggy Pop is an American rock singer
Les Paul was an American guitarist

explanation.surface: A pop singer and Les Paul, the guitarist, are mostly having a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is not a genre but Iggy Pop's surname, so Pop singer gives IGGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Giggles are fits of silly, nervous laughter.

clue.text: Ring doctor's surgery for treatment

definitions.note: the definition describes the purpose: something used for treatment

parts.note: an eye is a small ring or loop, as in hook and eye
OP is short for operation, surgery

explanation.surface: Ring the doctor's surgery to book treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye drops are a liquid medicine dispensed as drops to treat eye conditions.

clue.text: Figure at a cost of millions

parts.note: bought for a price means at a cost of
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A sum quoted at a price running into millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Form and figure both mean shape or outline of the body.

clue.text: Second home acquired by mum

indicators.note: taken into, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: mum means silent, mute
at home means in

explanation.surface: A second home is bought by someone's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother; it means quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute and a second are both very short spans of time, as in 'wait a second'.

clue.text: Curtail break and work to go over puzzle

indicators.note: going over means turning back on itself, so the combined letters are read backwards
to curtail is to cut short, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a break is a rest
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Advice to cut a break short and get back to working through a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtail' takes the T from REST, leaving RES; RES plus OP read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a difficult question or problem, a puzzle.

clue.text: Naive set off without good food

parts.note: green means inexperienced, naive

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to set off is to start; he began

explanation.surface: An innocent sets out on a journey taking nothing good to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes G from BEGAN, leaving BEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A green bean is a vegetable, the edible pod of the French bean.

clue.text: They might have rain in north — declaration after batting for both sides

parts.words: declaration after batting for both sides
parts.note: batting for both sides is slang for being bisexual, so the declaration is 'I'm bi'

explanation.surface: Cricket in the north: the team might face rain, with a declaration after both sides have batted.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides a coming-out: 'I'm bi'. In cricket a declaration ends an innings early.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are rain clouds, plural of nimbus.

clue.text: Kept tiger, male, without fences, living close to ground

indicators.note: each word loses its bounding letters, like a field stripped of fences

explanation.surface: A captive tiger, a male, is kept without fences and stays low to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, epigeal describes creatures or plant parts that live or grow on or just above the soil.

clue.text: Pack short underwear that's wild

parts.note: to pack is to cram or ram in

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: pants are underwear

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs skimpy underwear into a case, and things get wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means unrestrained, growing or spreading out of control.

clue.text: Actor might wear this coat on musical

indicators.note: here signals one piece placed after the other

parts.note: Grease is a stage and film musical
a coat is a layer of paint

explanation.surface: An actor might wear a coat in a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' looks like clothing; it is a layer of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasepaint is the thick theatrical make-up worn by performers on stage.
